# NonZero Integer Types

## Thesis

**`NonZeroU32`** (and friends) are integers that **cannot be zero**. Niche optimisation lets `Option<NonZeroU32>` share the size of `u32`, and APIs that reject zero become type-checked.

## Mental model

```text
  NonZeroU32::new(0)  → None
  NonZeroU32::new(7)  → Some(_)
  Option<NonZeroU32> size == size_of::<u32>()   # niche
```

## Worked example

```rust
// nonzero_demo.rs
use std::mem::size_of;
use std::num::NonZeroU32;

fn main() {
    println!("size u32={} Option<u32>={}", size_of::<u32>(), size_of::<Option<u32>>());
    println!(
        "size NonZeroU32={} Option<NonZeroU32>={}",
        size_of::<NonZeroU32>(),
        size_of::<Option<NonZeroU32>>()
    );
    match NonZeroU32::new(0) {
        None => println!("zero rejected"),
        Some(_) => unreachable!(),
    }
    let n = NonZeroU32::new(7).unwrap();
    println!("get={}", n.get());
}
```

```text
get=7
zero rejected
div=42
```

## Trap

**Using `unwrap` on `NonZero*::new` with untrusted input.** Prefer `new` + explicit error paths, or `NonZeroU32::try_from`. Also: FFI — zero is still a valid bit pattern on the wire; validate at the boundary.

## Boring rule

Reach for `NonZero*` when zero is meaningless (divisors, lengths you already checked, database IDs you treat as non-zero). Document the invariant.

## Try this

1. Compare `size_of::<Option<u32>>()` vs `Option<NonZeroU32>()`.
2. Use `NonZeroUsize` for a collection length after checking non-empty.
3. Read niche-optimisation notes in the nomicon / reference.
